'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
***[[2021 Kabul Airlift]]
****The [[Taliban]] calls for international commercial flights at the [[Kabul International Airport]] to resume after the airport was closed for evacuations. [https://www.urdupoint.com/en/world/kabul-airport-ready-to-open-for-international-1360360.html (UrduPoint)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**Five [[Palestinians]] are killed in [[Biddu, Jerusalem]], and two more are killed in [[Burqin, Palestine|Burqin]] during overnight [[military raid]]s by [[Israeli soldiers]]. Two soldiers are also injured during one of the raids. According to Israeli officials, the Palestinians were members of a [[Hamas]] [[clandestine cell system|cell]] who were planning large-scale [[kidnapping]]s and [[murder]]s across the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/26/two-palestinians-killed-by-israeli-forces-in-occupied-west-bank (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/hamas-cell-hit-in-west-bank-raids-planned-massive-jerusalem-terror-attack-tv/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[Communal conflicts in Nigeria]], [[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**Gunmen raid the village of Madamai in [[Kaduna State]], killing 34 people and wounding seven more. Two suspects are arrested. In [[Sokoto State]], 22 security personnel are killed by [[Islamic State – West Africa Province|ISWAP]] [[terrorist]]s during an attack on a remote [[army base]]. Other gunmen in Kaduna then also attacked a church, resulting in the death of a person and the wounding of others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/27/gunmen-kill-34-people-in-northwest-nigeria (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Five people are killed and six more are injured during a [[mass shooting]] at a public venue in [[Tumaco]], [[Colombia]]. A military commander has blamed the attack on [[FARC dissidents]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58706901 (BBC News)]
*[[2020–2021 Ethiopian–Sudanese clashes]]
**[[Sudan]] claims that it has repelled an advance by [[Ethiopian troops]] into Umm Barakit District, [[al-Fashaga]]. However, [[Ethiopia]] denies any movement of its forces on the [[Ethiopia–Sudan border]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58698010 (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[74th Tony Awards]]
**''[[Moulin Rouge! (musical)|Moulin Rouge!]]'' wins 10 [[Tony Awards]] at the 74th Tony Awards, including [[Tony Award for Best Musical|Best Musical]]. Additionally, ''[[The Inheritance (play)|The Inheritance]]'' by [[Matthew Lopez (writer)|Matthew Lopez]] wins [[Tony Award for Best Play|Best Play]] and ''[[A Soldier's Play]]'' by [[Charles Fuller]] wins [[Tony Award for Best Revival of a Play|Best Revival of a Play]]. [https://www.npr.org/2021/09/26/1040804568/tony-awards-2021-inheritance-best-play-moulin-rouge (NPR)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021 United Kingdom fuel panic buying]]
**[[Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy|UK Business Secretary]] [[Kwasi Kwarteng]] announces the [[oil industry]] will be exempted from the [[Competition Act 1998]] so that companies can coordinate and deliver [[petroleum product]]s easier in light of fuel shortages brought on by [[panic buying]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-58701620 (BBC News)]
*[[Prime Minister of Peru|Peruvian prime minister]] [[Guido Bellido]] warns companies which drill for gas in the country to either pay higher taxes or face [[nationalization]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-pm-warns-gas-sector-pay-higher-taxes-or-face-nationalization-2021-09-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[List of earthquakes in 2021|Earthquakes in 2021]]
**An [[earthquake]] of [[Seismic magnitude scales|magnitude]] 5.7 strikes [[Occidental Mindoro]], [[Philippines]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/26/magnitude-5-7-earthquake-hits-south-of-philippines-capital (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana]]
****[[Ghana]] receives 1.5 million doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]] donated by [[Germany]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/ghana-receives-15m-doses-of-astrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine-from-germany/2375540 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] lifts its nighttime curfew, but imposes [[Immunity passport#COVID-19|vaccine certificate]]s for public events as the number of cases declines. [https://north-africa.com/2021/09/covid-19-tunisia-lifts-nighttime-curfew-as-virus-cases-fall/ (''The North African Journal'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
****[[Texas]] surpasses four million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.dallasnews.com/news/public-health/2021/09/26/texas-surpasses-4-million-total-covid-19-cases/ (''The Dallas Morning News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
***[[Singapore]] reports a record 1,939 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 87,592. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/2-seniors-die-of-covid-19-bringing-death-toll-to-78-1939-new-cases-in-spore (''The Straits Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Human rights violations by the CIA]]
**[[Yahoo! News]] reports that members of the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] (CIA), including  then-[[Director of the Central Intelligence Agency|Director]] [[Mike Pompeo]], planned in 2017 to kidnap or potentially assassinate [[WikiLeaks]] founder [[Julian Assange]] for leaking [[Vault 7|documents describing hacking tools]] used by the CIA. *[[Kosovo–Serbia relations]]
**[[2021 North Kosovo protests]]
***The [[Serbia]]n government accuses [[Kosovo]] of "provocations" after it mobilized its special [[Kosovo Police|police units]] to the border, and places the [[Serbian Army]] on a heightened state of alert. The police units were mobilized after hundreds of [[Kosovo Serbs]] staged daily protests and blockaded roads connected to the two border crossings between the two countries after the [[Kosovar government]] passed a law requiring that Serbia-registered vehicles wear temporary license plates when entering the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/26/serbian-troops-on-heightened-alert-at-kosovo-border (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Palestinian Legislative Council]] member [[Khalida Jarrar]] is released from [[Israel]]i prison after nearly two years in detention. She was [[criminal charge|charged]] for her affiliation with the [[left-wing]] political party [[Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine]], which is considered an illegal organization in Israel. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/26/palestinian-mp-khalida-jarrar-released-from-israeli-prison (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Taliban]]'s [[Ministry for the Propagation of Virtue and the Prevention of Vice (Afghanistan)|religious police]] orders barbers in [[Afghanistan]]'s [[Helmand Province]] and [[Kabul]] to stop trimming beards. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58700159 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 German federal election]]
**Germans head to the polls to elect the new [[Bundestag]], as well as a new [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] to succeed [[Angela Merkel]], who is stepping down [[Chancellorship of Angela Merkel|after 16 years in power]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/26/german-election-polls-open-tight-race-elect-new-chancellor (Al Jazeera)]
**Projections show the centre-left [[Social Democratic Party of Germany]] (SPD) narrowly beating the governing centre-right [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany]] (CDU) in the popular vote by 1.7 percentage points, with the latter on course for its worst showing since the end of [[World War II]]. Both parties claim the mandate for the Chancellorship. [https://www.politico.eu/article/election-germany-results-limbo/ (''Politico.eu'')]
**[[Alliance 90/The Greens|The Greens]] and [[Free Democratic Party (Germany)|Free Democratic Party]] made enough gains to form a possible [[coalition government]] with either the CDU or the SPD. [https://www.npr.org/2021/09/27/1040846060/germany-elections-update-coalition-cdu-spd-green-fdp? (NPR)]
*[[2021 Icelandic parliamentary election]]
**The final results of yesterday's election in [[Iceland]] show that the ruling left-[[right wing|right]] [[coalition]] strengthened [[Parliamentary majority|its majority]] despite [[Prime Minister of Iceland|Prime Minister]] [[Katrín Jakobsdóttir]] losing ground. The [[Independence Party (Iceland)|Independence Party]] won the most seats, with 16. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/icelands-ruling-coalition-boosts-majority-preliminary-election-results-show-2021-09-26/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Swiss same-sex marriage referendum]], [[LGBT rights in Switzerland]]
**Citizens in [[Switzerland]] cast their final vote on whether to legalize [[same-sex marriage]] in the country. Although [[civil unions]] have been legal since 2007, recent polls showed a solid backing for the proposition. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210926-switzerland-goes-to-the-polls-in-same-sex-marriage-referendum (France 24)]
*[[2021 Sammarinese abortion referendum]], [[Abortion in San Marino]]
**[[San Marino]] citizens vote in a [[referendum]] on the [[Legalization of abortion|legalization]] of [[abortion]] up to 12 weeks of pregnancy or in cases where the health of the mother or fetus is at risk. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/sep/26/san-marino-votes-in-referendum-on-lifting-abortion-ban (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2021 Tunisian political crisis]]
**Around 2,000 [[Tunisians]] protest in front of the [[National Theatre of Tunisia|National Theatre]] in the capital of [[Tunis]] to demand the [[resignation]] of [[President of Tunisia|President]] [[Kais Saied]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/26/hundreds-gather-in-tunisia-to-oppose-president-saieds-power-grab (Al Jazeera)]
